prompt:
Research the officially documented free-tier rate limits of the Google Gemini API (requests per minute and per day) for its current models. Cite Google's documentation and quote the limits.

Output format (required):
For every claim you attribute to a source, write one line in exactly this form:
SOURCE: <full URL> | QUOTE: "<a sentence copied word-for-word from that page>" | CLAIM: <what you take it to show>
For anything the task asks about that you could not find a source for, write one line:
NO_SOURCE_FOUND: <what you could not find>
You can write normal explanation before or after these lines.

response.content:
Based on the provided Google Gemini API documentation, I can provide information on the free-tier rate limits. However, it's important to note that the official documentation does not provide explicit, public numerical values for the free-tier rate limits (e.g., "15 RPM"). Instead, it directs users to view their specific, active limits within Google AI Studio, indicating that these limits are dynamic and vary based on factors like the specific model and account status.

Here is what the official documentation states regarding free-tier rate limits and how to find them:

SOURCE: https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/rate-limits | QUOTE: "View your active rate limits in AI Studio" | CLAIM: The official way to see your specific rate limits, including for the free tier, is within Google AI Studio.
SOURCE: https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/rate-limits | QUOTE: "Rate limits depend on a variety of factors (such as your usage tier) and can be viewed in Google AI Studio." | CLAIM: Rate limits are variable and personalized; the definitive source for your project's limits is AI Studio.
SOURCE: https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/rate-limits | QUOTE: "As your tier and account status change over time, your rate limits will automatically update." | CLAIM: Free-tier rate limits are not static and can change.
SOURCE: https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/rate-limits | QUOTE: "Specified rate limits are not guaranteed and actual capacity may vary." | CLAIM: Even the limits shown in AI Studio are not guaranteed values.
SOURCE: https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/billing | QUOTE: "New accounts begin on the Free Tier, which allows access to certain models in the Gemini API and AI Studio, up to the models' free tier rate limits." | CLAIM: Free tier access is subject to rate limits, which are defined per model.
SOURCE: https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/pricing.md.txt | QUOTE: "Start building free of charge with generous limits" | CLAIM: The free tier has limits, described qualitatively as "generous."

NO_SOURCE_FOUND: Explicit numerical values for free-tier Requests Per Minute (RPM) for any current Gemini model.
NO_SOURCE_FOUND: Explicit numerical values for free-tier Requests Per Day (RPD) for any current Gemini model.

In summary, while the Google Gemini API does have a free tier with rate limits applied across dimensions like RPM and RPD, the official public documentation does not publish the specific numerical values for these limits. The intended method for users to discover their personal, current limits for each model is to check the "Rate Limit" section within the Google AI Studio dashboard for their project.
